gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns incorrect extended-real conditions in the A-characterization, whereas the gold defect is the unsupported converse from bare specular differentiability to existence of both one-sided derivatives, exposed by oscillating quotients. It does not recognize that missing necessity implication.

The gold issue is that the scaled derivative used by the quasi-MVT can be undefined despite specular differentiability. ISSUE-003 instead addresses extended-infinite endpoint cases in the A-equivalence and does not diagnose nonexistence of the composite scaled derivative caused by oscillation.

Both identify the invalid deletion of the sign/absolute value in the scalar quasi-MVT proof, which falsely supports the lower bound by derivative magnitudes; both recognize that only signed information and the upper estimate survive.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The norm-valued two-sided quasi-MVT lower bound is unsupported because the scalar argument controls the signed difference, not its positive magnitude without a sign choice.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof replaces the signed endpoint difference by its norm and thereby asserts a false lower bound by derivative magnitudes.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly identifies the invalid sign deletion, supplies a counterexample to the infimum bound, and repairs it by retaining signed pairings or deleting the lower bound.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false unbiasedness equality equating the expectation of sampled component specular gradients with the specular gradient of the finite-sum objective, due to nonlinearity.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Uniform component sampling does not generally produce an unbiased estimator of the aggregate specular gradient; averaging component specular gradients differs from applying the nonlinear specular-gradient operation to the average.

component_coverage.gold_component: The component-sampling estimator equality is false for the advertised finite-sum class, invalidating the method's unbiasedness interface and dependent convergence theorem.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-010 states the nonlinearity, gives an explicit finite-sum counterexample, identifies the violated contract and theorem dependency, and proposes the appropriate relaxed subgradient-inclusion interface.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the missing upper bound on the specular-gradient norm needed to infer divergence of the normalized step sum from divergence of the t-step sum, and both give the bounded-iterates/local-Lipschitz repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The liminf contradiction requires proving uniformly bounded specular gradients so that h_l=t_l/||nabla^s f(x_l)|| is bounded below by a constant multiple of t_l.

component_coverage.gold_component: The liminf contradiction is unsupported because H3 controls sum t_l, not sum h_l, until gradient boundedness is established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-011 explicitly identifies the missing gradient bound, explains why it is needed, and supplies the same boundedness/local-Lipschitz argument and repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid transfer from convergence of a subsequence to closeness of every sufficiently late iterate, and both repair it by starting the tail estimate at a sufficiently late subsequence index.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof incorrectly treats subsequence convergence as full-sequence convergence without first selecting a suitable subsequence iterate as the telescoping starting point.

component_coverage.gold_component: The final convergence step does not establish convergence of the full iterate sequence from subsequence convergence alone.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-012 directly identifies the invalid all-iterates inference and gives the correct subsequence-indexed telescoping repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the sample-dependent normalized step cannot be factored out of the conditional expectation, so the proof's cross term incorrectly uses the unnormalized unbiasedness relation and the descent inequality does not follow.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Normalization makes the stochastic step depend on the sampled component, changing the conditional cross term from an unnormalized expected gradient to an expectation of normalized directions and invalidating the claimed descent estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The conditional descent proof incorrectly factors out the sample-dependent normalized step and substitutes the unnormalized unbiasedness identity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-014 explicitly identifies the measurability/factorization error, writes the actual normalized cross term, gives a counterexample, and explains that normalization destroys expected descent.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-014 concerns the separate normalization/measurability error in the descent expansion. It does not identify the gold issue's logical error: a weighted sum bound yields a minimum or selected-index bound, not a bound for every or unspecified index.
